exercises.title: Find and Union
exercises.task: Fill Find (follow the parents up to the root, and on the way back point each element straight at it) and Union (join the two roots, the smaller group under the bigger). The last check links 200 000 elements: without one of the two tricks it never finishes.
hints: Find is three lines of recursion: if d.parent[x] == x return x; otherwise root := d.Find(d.parent[x]), then d.parent[x] = root.
In Union: return false when ra == rb. Swap so that d.size[ra] >= d.size[rb], then d.parent[rb] = ra and add the sizes.

exercises.title: The cheapest network (Kruskal)
exercises.task: Connect every machine for the least total cable. Kruskal's rule: look at the links from the cheapest up, and keep one only if it joins two machines that are not connected yet. "Already connected?" is exactly what union-find answers, in almost constant time. Fill the two holes of Cheapest.
hints: d.Union(l.A, l.B) both answers "were they separate?" and joins them.
A tree on n machines has n-1 links: if fewer were chosen, something is unreachable.
